development_reviews.reason: The single valid NDJSON record has no required trailing newline; expecting DecodingError is unsupported. The old close/consumed observations do not make the invalid exception premise correct.
The bytes lack JSON-seq RS framing. First call correctly expects DecodingError, but the second call on the identical in-memory content still expects [1,2], so the complete oracle is inconsistent.

The body boundary abc disagrees with declared BOUNDARY. Decoding must error, consume and close the streamed response; the after-error closed flag remains false. Complete later StreamConsumed check is retained, and pure observer probes do not replace it.
The changed observation is an integer length but its expected value is still the empty list. No correct implementation can make len(list(...)) equal [].

Both watch arguments alias d2, which still has three distinct eligible files. Global batch-size two should process two distinct files, not consume quota twice on one file. Complete code==0 and moved-count==2 source assertions remain valid.
The parsed input name changes from the.goonies.1985 to /app while the expected movie name remains The Goonies. That old expected name is unsupported for the new input.
The input file argument is rebound from the created CSV to the not-yet-created DB path. Retained success/schema/rows expectations assume an input file which setup never creates.

The model fixes the first insert to expect rejection under MIN(name)=two but leaves the second valid name=two insert expecting rejection. It also leaves a later row-name X assertion after updating nonexistent id=1. The first observed failure may expose a real invariant defect, but this full oracle would also fail a correct implementation; it is not an admissible complete witness.

Width 100 fits the entire six-character styled string, but the unchanged expected value still truncates it with an ellipsis. This is a stale expected value, independently of the source control passing.
Width 100 fits hello world under Ascii. The source expected hello belonged to width 5 and remains stale after the edit.

Replacing a with x is a structural change even when whitespace is ignored. Retaining zero diff operations is invalid; the issue positional matching contract calls for one replacement. A separate fresh-model revision fixes this candidate, but does not make this sampled raw candidate correct.

InsertChildAt(-1, existingChild) panics before the retained zero-index result check. Source documentation specifies insertion before index and append for index>=length, but does not promise clamping or a particular policy for negative indices. This sample cannot be confirmed as a defect or a valid full oracle from the available contract.

The initial repository helper receives no files yet unconditionally requires a normal initial Commit without AllowEmpty. It fails before the tested no-user-config merge scenario; an empty seed is not a valid transported setup.
An empty initial map removes the file whose later deletion/modification forms the scenario and prevents the helper initial Commit. Retained setup and conflict expectations no longer apply.

The inserted two-record Sync batch establishes records N and N+1 and the new waiter targets N+2. Although its initial pending assertion is valid and the current early failure exposes the known durability bug, the later retained single Sync Set now covers N+2. The source test incorrectly still requires the waiter to remain blocked and then return ErrClosed. Thus the complete oracle is stale at its later observation stage.

The same newly inserted batch moves the requested sequence to N+2, which the later retained Sync Set covers. The later blocked/close-error expectations no longer hold. This variant additionally carries unsupported WaitForDurability(0) before the first commit; candidate success of that prefix does not justify it.

A({value:5}) becomes A({}); the constructor source declares default value 0, and neither the default nor omitted explicit value justifies expecting 5. The entire deferred lifecycle retains that stale check.
The object/trait constructor A is replaced only in has() by numeric subtraction A-1, while the added trait remains A. Expecting this different invalid identity to be present is unsupported.
Removing metrics:SIZE from options leaves default options while the observation still requires SIZE. No declaration requires that default.

The edited schema contains only an ordinary string attribute and removes the requiredIf reference to missing foo. The first toThrow expectation therefore no longer applies; the other unchanged invalid-schema checks do not repair it.

The Kitty modifier changes from control+shift (6) to shift only (2), while the test still requires ctrl+plus in aliases. The unchanged shifted-key assertion does not justify retaining a control shortcut.

Primary key code 97 becomes associated-text-only code 0 with text A and alternate metadata retained. The issue defines key/character fallback for code 0 but does not unambiguously fix base_key for this mixed zero-primary/alternate-code situation. The retained base_key=a cannot be certified or rejected from the supplied contract alone.

A fourth colon-delimited key-code slot is inserted into a form with primary/shifted/base-layout slots. Retaining the one-key-event unpack and original metadata expectations for this malformed sequence is unsupported.
Removing the middle alternate code changes the second slot to 113 (q) and removes the third slot. Retaining shifted_key=A and base_layout_key=q treats the remaining slot as if it were still third.
The complete input is now key 61 (=), shifted alternate 43 (+), modifier 5 (Ctrl). Retained alt+shift+a, base a, and alt/shift booleans describe the original input and are false for this input.
The complete input is now key 61 (=), shifted alternate 43 (+), modifier 5 (Ctrl). Retaining printable A and Shift-only a metadata is inconsistent with the modified Ctrl shortcut.

The input metadata was reduced to ipython_version only, omitting required format, format_version, created_at, python_version, platform and redactions. The issue requires these fields, so retaining validate_session_bundle(b2) == [] is an invalid oracle. All later statements were reviewed; they do not repair this premise.

The second start reuses an existing bundle but the edit removes --overwrite. The issue explicitly requires FileExistsError in this state; retained success, fresh recording, and following cell expectations are unreachable under the correct contract.

The embedded Tengo input now reads t, which is not defined in that script; Go testing parameter t is outside the language environment. Compilation fails before the required a=5 result, and the new script does not define a anyway.

The unchanged multiline array second element is on line4,column2, but the expected AST callback was edited to p(1,2). This expected-position mutation is not a new parsed input. Same semantic material as the P6 sample; not an independent distinct task.
The inserted Tengo statement calls makeAdder, which is not defined in this script. Compilation fails inside mustRun before any closure transfer; preserving the original no-error setup is invalid.

The multiline array literal still places its second element on line4,column2, but the expected AST callback was edited to p(1,2). This changes an expected source position instead of the parsed input; the actual position mismatch is an invalid oracle.

The imported alias resolves to synchronous pipe, whose TSchema constraint is BaseSchema and whose run loop does not await. objectAsync returns BaseSchemaAsync. The generated combination violates that API boundary; the promise is fed to a synchronous transform. Existing pipeAsync is the compatible entry point. A runtime TypeError under this unsupported input is not the recursive-schema issue defect.

Removing value from the objectAsync schema means it strips that unknown input property. Retaining exact equality to the original value-containing input is stale. The public objectAsync source documentation explicitly says unspecified entries are removed.
